incident-bot: Paging on-call: Dedicated pool 'zarafa-enterprise-prod' reporting GPU queue depth > 95% and token latency SLO violations. alert_id=DP-EXH-7231 :rotating_light:

alex (oncall): I'm on it. Checking metrics now — which tenant is affected?

maya (sre): It's the Zarafa dedicated pool, single-tenant. Seeing steady ramp in long-running streaming calls from their internal batch workers.

ian (eng-oncall): Logs show a surge of 6.5k concurrent sessions starting 02:12 UTC. Autoscaler didn't add capacity because burst is disabled for that pool.

alex (oncall): Can we enable temporary burst to shared overflow? What's the protocol for enterprise pools?

maya (sre): Prod runbook section 3: for single-tenant dedicated pools we can enable "overflow-burst" if customer contract allows emergency burst. Need ENG-OPS + CS approval.

lina (cs): Zarafa CS confirms emergency burst is approved for up to 60m under their support contract. I'll notify the account immediately and own comms.

ian (eng-oncall): Good. Technical checklist before bursting: 1) confirm fallback model available 2) set tenant throttles for non-critical job classes 3) enable burst flag and validate routing.

alex (oncall): I'll throttle background workers for Zarafa via runtime policy. Command applying now:
```
# throttle policy
redwoodctl policies apply --tenant zarafa --policy background=10rps
```

maya (sre): Throttle applied, queue depth dropped 18% within 90s. Background job rate now 10rps.

ops-bot: evictor-scan: identified 4 candidate low-prio tasks (priority=LOW) across pool. Recommend graceful termination to free one GPU.

ian (eng-oncall): We're still at ~88% GPU utilization after throttle. Ready to enable burst. I need a thumbs up from alex + lina for CS ack.

alex (oncall): Ack from me.

lina (cs): CS acked, Zarafa informed and accepts 45m emergency burst. They'll hold off heavy ingestion jobs on their side.

maya (sre): Initiating burst. Enabling overflow to shared-capacity with isolation tags. Command:
```
redwoodctl pool burst-enable --pool zarafa-enterprise-prod --duration 45m --isolation=tenant-priority
```

incident-bot: Action logged: burst-enable by maya at 1775556798. change_id=BURST-9991

ian (eng-oncall): Routing tests OK. New sessions landed on overflow nodes, no cross-tenant KV contamination. Latency improving.

alex (oncall): Monitoring token cost bump — expected. Keep an eye on unit economics, we'll reconcile on postmortem.

lina (cs): I've opened a customer incident case and emailed Zarafa with the mitigation summary and ETA. They asked for updates every 15m.

maya (sre): Current metrics (02:26 UTC): GPU util 62%, 99th latency back under SLO, queue depth dropping. Burst holding.

ian (eng-oncall): We're seeing a recurring pattern where their scheduled ingestion at 02:10 spikes capacity by ~6k sessions. Recommend we add a schedule-aware throttle in their tenant policy to prevent recurrence.

alex (oncall): Agree. Action items: (1) keep burst on for 45m, (2) create tenant schedule throttle, (3) follow-up postmortem with model-routing suggestions and quota changes.

lina (cs): I'll coordinate with Zarafa to move their ingestion later and add pre-check gating.

ops-bot: burst timer set: 2700s remaining. automated rollback scheduled.

maya (sre): Note for post-incident: autoscaler didn't trigger because dedicated pools require burst flag in config to allow expansion; we should evaluate an emergency autoscale path for enterprise pools.

alex (oncall): Oncall handoff — I'm handing to maya for watch. I'll update incident doc and start timeline.

maya (sre): Taking watch. I'll keep updates here every 10m until burst ends.

incident-bot: Update: burst will auto-disable at 1775559458 unless extended.

lina (cs): Zarafa acknowledges and thanks the team. No visible user-facing failures reported from their side beyond transient timeouts.

maya (sre): 02:40 UTC — metrics stable, preparing to let burst expire. I'll run cleanup script 5m before disable.

ian (eng-oncall): Cleanup executed. Reverted temporary throttles after observing safe steady state.

ops-bot: burst-disable logged at 1775557860. change_id=BURST-9991-ROLLBACK

alex (oncall): Closing loop: burst ran 18m effective, reduced latency breaches to zero. Postmortem owner: ian. CS follow-up: lina. Action items assigned in incident doc. :white_check_mark:
